chief_complaint: Uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension with comorbid HIV infection and multiple cardiometabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58-year-old man with long‑standing HIV infection managed on a darunavir/ritonavir‑based regimen. Over the past years he has developed obesity, pre‑diabetes, anemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. Recent vital signs show severe hypertension (159/112 mmHg) despite no antihypertensive therapy documented. Social stressors including part‑time employment, exposure to violence, and chronic stress are noted, and outpatient follow‑up for chronic disease management appears limited. Laboratory data are incomplete (no lipid panel, renal function, or repeat hemoglobin values).

active_problems.name: Reports of violence in the environment

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include a history of appendectomy (1984), prior full‑time employment, social isolation, and two minor hand lacerations in 2018. Medication review reminders were documented and resolved. No other chronic resolved diagnoses are present.

active_medications.name: lamivudine 300 MG / tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 MG Oral Tablet

social_determinants: Part‑time employment, reports of violence in the environment, chronic stress, rural residence in Berkshire County, MA; limited outpatient follow‑up; potential socioeconomic instability.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 2 hypertension (SBP 159, DBP 112), obesity, HIV‑associated inflammation, and likely dyslipidemia (lipid labs missing). Metabolic risk: prediabetes (A1c 5.9%), obesity, protease‑inhibitor therapy. Renal risk: tenofovir exposure and anemia with no eGFR data. Hematologic risk: chronic anemia. Pulmonary/sleep risk: obstructive sleep apnea (no CPAP documented). Immunologic risk: chronic HIV infection (Charlson index 1). Psychosocial risk: part‑time employment, environmental violence, stress. Overall clinical complexity rated moderate.

clinical_impression: The patient is a middle‑aged man with well‑controlled HIV on a protease‑inhibitor regimen but with a high burden of cardiometabolic risk: severe untreated hypertension, obesity, pre‑diabetes, anemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. Social stressors and limited outpatient engagement likely contribute to suboptimal management of these comorbidities. Immediate priorities include initiating antihypertensive therapy, completing metabolic and renal labs, addressing sleep apnea treatment, and improving chronic disease follow‑up.
